# Hydra
English | 中文
Hydra is an unofficial community fork of DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`), the open-source agent harness dev
eloped by DeepSeek. It keeps the upstream **everything-is-a-plugin** architecture, powered by Cordis
, and adds plugins for long-running goals, research journals, learning memory, and models with weak
tool calling such as GLM, Qwen, and local models.
Hydra is built on DeepSeek Harness. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by DeepSeek
. "DeepSeek Harness" is a trademark of DeepSeek and is used here only to describe what Hydra is buil
t on. Read the disclaimer before you use it.

## Disclaimer
Hydra is an independent community project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or
supported by DeepSeek, Anthropic, OpenAI, or any other model provider. DeepSeek, DeepSeek Harness, C
laude, and other product names are trademarks of their respective owners and appear here only to ide
ntify the software Hydra is built on or works with.
Hydra is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, under the MIT License. To the fullest exten
t permitted by law, its authors and contributors are not liable for any claim, damages, data loss, s
ecurity incident, or cost arising from its use.
Hydra runs AI agents that can execute shell commands, change or delete files, and send your code, pr
ompts, and files to the model providers you configure. You are responsible for:

- reviewing what the agent does, and keeping backups of anything important;
- your API keys and the
data you send to those providers and the laws that apply to it.
Model output can be wrong. Nothing Hydra produces, including its research and market data tools, is
financial, legal, medical, or other professional advice. Read the safety notice and report security
problems as SECURITY.md describes.
## Credits
- DeepSeek Harness, Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek, released under the MIT License. This repository kee

ps the upstream history: every upstream commit is here, and Hydra's changes sit on top of it.
- Cord

is, vendored by upstream; see vendor/README.md.
- Third-party dependencies and their licenses are li
sted in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
## What Hydra adds
| Area | What it does |
| Claude out of the box | The Web and desktop app ship the Anthropic route with Claude Opus 5.5, Son
net 5.5, and Haiku 5.5, and new sessions use Claude Sonnet 5.5. The first-run step asks for an API k
ey instead of a DeepSeek account sign-in; the desktop welcome lets you pick Anthropic, DeepSeek, Ope

nAI, or another provider for that key (`dsh-web-app`, `dsh-client-ui-settings-models`). |
| Tool cal
ling for GLM, Qwen, and local models | Arguments are coerced before validation, and the shell tools

no longer require the UI-only `description` argument (`dsh-tools`, `dsh-tool-bash`). |
| Turns that
keep going | A max-output stop continues by itself, a context-length error triggers compaction and a
retry instead of ending the turn, and a summary that comes back without text is retried (`dsh-auto-

continue`, `dsh-compaction-basic`). |
| Goals that run for days | No round cap, retries with backoff
after request errors, and an independent check of the model's "complete" claim. Opening a session n

ever restarts a goal; `/goal resume` does (`dsh-goal-evaluator`). |
| Research journals | `/research
<objective>` keeps a discovery journal of breakthroughs, hypotheses, experiments, dead ends, and ne
xt steps, recalled into every request. `/research list` and `/research continue <name>` pick a journ

al up in a new session (`dsh-research`). |
| Learning memory | Notes are extracted at the end of a t
urn and scoped to the project they came from. `/learn` approves, rejects, or promotes them to skills
, `/learn from <path>` imports files, repeated notes merge as they are stored, and `/learn consolida

te` rewrites related notes into fewer current ones (`dsh-memory`, `dsh-learning`). |
| Knowledge bas

e | `/kb` indexes folders into a local full-text index the model can search (`dsh-knowledge`). |
| R
esumable workflows | A workflow run cut off by a lost connection or a spent budget resumes without p

aying again for the steps that finished (`dsh-workflow-journal`). |
[该节后续省略]
## What Hydra leaves out
Hydra's Web and desktop app ship these upstream features disabled, because they serve DeepSeek's own
account and data collection:
| Feature | Rows disabled |

| The DeepSeek account settings section and account menu | `ui-settings-account` |
| Like/Dislike an
d `/feedback`, whose submission also released a Session-log slice to DeepSeek's telemetry collector

| `message-feedback`, `command-feedback`, `ui-message-feedback` |
| Session-log upload with requests
to the official DeepSeek API, and its Settings switch | `session-log-deepseek`, `ui-settings-sessio

n-log` |
| Desktop usage analytics, which upstream sends to DeepSeek's telemetry collector with no u
ser-facing control | none: `product-analytics` stays loaded with `enabled: false` |
The desktop welcome asks for a provider API key and offers no DeepSeek account sign-in. DeepSeek API
keys still work through `llm-deepseek`. The CLI and SDK profiles keep these rows, and there the upl
oad goes only with requests to DeepSeek's official API. A profile patch row with the row's `id` and
`disabled: false` turns a feature back on; for analytics, the patch row restates the `product-analyt
ics` row's `config` with `enabled: true`.
## Requirements

- Node.js 22.19 or newer, or 24 or newer (`node --version`).
- pnpm 11.7.0 through Corepack, which s

hips with Node.js: run `corepack enable` once.
- Git 2.26 or newer.
- A C compiler for the native ad

don: `gcc` or `clang` on Linux, the Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS (`xcode-select --install`).
-
A model: an Anthropic API key for Claude, a DeepSeek API key, another hosted API, or any OpenAI-comp
atible server such as vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, or LM Studio.
